newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus lashes out at West.
newsitem.headline: Belarus lashes out at West.

text.p: Belarus lashed out at the West on Tuesday, accusing a group of European ambassadors based in the capital Minsk of gross interference in its internal affairs.

The leading commentator on state television, which is controlled by President Alexander Lukashenko, said the ambassadors of Britain, Italy, Germany and France had issued a joint statement to the foreign ministry on Monday.

"The initiative is a gross interference in the internal affairs of a sovereign state," Alexander Zimovski said on the main evening news bulletin, saying he had only received a text of the statement on Tuesday.
A spokeswoman for the British embassy confirmed a group of ambassadors had launched an initiative on Monday but gave few details and declined to comment on the protest.
"The ambassador did go to the foreign ministry...and expressed concern about recent developments here and their implications," she said by telephone.
The other embassies were not immediately available for comment.
Zimovksi, who heads a flagship current affairs programme on Sundays, is considered an informal spokesman for Lukashenko, who was due to meet President Boris Yeltsin in Moscow on Wednesday.

The two leaders plan to discuss integration between their two states, which were split by the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, and the political situation in Belarus, a Kremlin spokesman said on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old Lukashenko, who has been accused by critics of taking an increasingly authoritarian line since coming to power two years ago, has said that Yeltsin had expressed support for his plan to hold a referendum to extend his term.
The commentator said the diplomats had criticised as undemocratic Lukashenko's moves to muster support for the referendum by holding an "All-Belarus" meeting on Saturday.
The meeting is part of Lukashenko's efforts to push through his plans to hold the referendum on November 7 which he hopes will give him a new five-year tenure into the next century.

Opposition members of parliament, who voted on Friday to go ahead with a separate referendum on November 24 that could abolish the post of president altogether, have said the meeting will be attended only by functionaries loyal to Lukashenko.
